$comment: W20 probe scene matrix — what Apple draws for RoundedRectangle(cornerRadius:style:.continuous)
when the radius exceeds 0.327083 of the short side. NOTHING else reads this file. It runs
through VITREA_SCENES into its own fixtures directory under
packages/calibration/results/2026-09-05-w20-capsule-corner/probe/, so the canonical
scenes.json and the frozen bed stay untouched. Both backgrounds reuse an existing kind
verbatim: nothing rebuilds and no TCC re-grant is needed for the rasters.
What it is for. vitrea's Apple reference clamps the RADIUS above the saturation ratio
1 / (2 * APPLE_REACH) = 0.327083, so that Apple's measured corner reach 1.52866495 * r still
fits half the short side (packages/geometry/src/apple.ts, buildAppleContour; pinned by
test/apple.test.ts under the name 'Apple's budget policy is its own'). That was never
measured — S2 fitted the corner below the ratio only, and the bed's capsules are Capsule(), a
circular stadium by definition, which cannot answer it (claims 5.83). These rungs put the
question to Apple: five radii on a 120 x 44 box from just below the ratio to the capsule
limit, three on the 44 x 44 box that is the toolbar's case, and Capsule() beside each as the
control whose true shape is known.
Untinted, state rest, 1x light-standard only. This measures a CONTOUR: the tint and the
colour scheme are noise on that axis, and a corner law is scale-free, so 1x is the whole
measurement rather than half of one. Two backgrounds because the contour is read two ways —
the checkerboard by a local-contrast silhouette and light-solid by the rim band's peak locus.
Nothing here is fitted to anything: every scene is 'recorded'.

light-solid.$comment: System light grey, the canonical bed's entry verbatim so the committed raster is reused and nothing rebuilds. The flat case: no backdrop detail, so the rim band reads alone and its peak locus is the contour.

checkerboard.$comment: The canonical bed's entry verbatim. Every cell edge is a step edge, so the material's blur shows as a collapse of LOCAL CONTRAST everywhere inside the surface — which is the silhouette rule this probe reads it with, and which the outer shadow does not trip because a darkened checker keeps its contrast.

rrect-120x44-r14.$comment: Ratio 0.3182, BELOW Apple's saturation ratio 0.327083 (= 1 / (2 * 1.52866495)): the reach 21.40 px still fits the corner's budget 22.00 px, so every candidate policy draws the same corner here. It is the ladder's control: the rung that tests the instrument rather than Apple.

rrect-120x44-r16.$comment: Ratio 0.3636, above saturation: the reach would be 24.46 px against a budget of 22.00 px, an overflow of 11.2 %. vitrea's policy today clamps the radius to 14.39 px; a shoulder compression would keep 16. The first rung above saturation.

rrect-120x44-r18.$comment: Ratio 0.4091, above saturation: the reach would be 27.52 px against a budget of 22.00 px, an overflow of 25.1 %. vitrea's policy today clamps the radius to 14.39 px; a shoulder compression would keep 18. Mid-ladder, where the two candidate policies are furthest apart per unit of overflow.

rrect-120x44-r20.$comment: Ratio 0.4545, above saturation: the reach would be 30.57 px against a budget of 22.00 px, an overflow of 39.0 %. vitrea's policy today clamps the radius to 14.39 px; a shoulder compression would keep 20.

rrect-120x44-r22.$comment: Ratio 0.5000, above saturation: the reach would be 33.63 px against a budget of 22.00 px, an overflow of 52.9 %. vitrea's policy today clamps the radius to 14.39 px; a shoulder compression would keep 22. The capsule limit reached by RoundedRectangle rather than by Capsule(). If Apple compresses the shoulder this must draw exactly the stadium the capsule control draws; if Apple clamps the radius it draws a rounded rectangle whose corner is a third smaller. The two are 7.6 px apart on the contour, fifteen times the grid's 0.5 px floor.

capsule-120x44.$comment: The control. `Capsule()` is a circular stadium by definition (`Sources/SceneViews.swift`), so this cell is what the contour reader is verified against before any rung is read, and it is what `rrect-120x44-r22` is compared to.

rrect-44x44-r14.$comment: Ratio 0.3182, BELOW Apple's saturation ratio 0.327083 (= 1 / (2 * 1.52866495)): the reach 21.40 px still fits the corner's budget 22.00 px, so every candidate policy draws the same corner here. The circle regime — the toolbar's 44 x 44 case — below saturation.

rrect-44x44-r18.$comment: Ratio 0.4091, above saturation: the reach would be 27.52 px against a budget of 22.00 px, an overflow of 25.1 %. vitrea's policy today clamps the radius to 14.39 px; a shoulder compression would keep 18. The square box's mid rung.

rrect-44x44-r22.$comment: Ratio 0.5000, above saturation: the reach would be 33.63 px against a budget of 22.00 px, an overflow of 52.9 %. vitrea's policy today clamps the radius to 14.39 px; a shoulder compression would keep 22. The square box at the limit: a circle of diameter 44 under a shoulder compression, a rounded square under vitrea's radius clamp. This is the shape the bed's `toolbar-group` draws.

capsule-44x44.$comment: `Capsule()` on a square box, which is a circle. The second control, and the shape the bed's `toolbar-group` items are declared as.

profiles.$comment: The probe's one profile, as W18's and W19's probes had one: this machine presents at 1x and the canonical 2x fixtures were captured on a reconfigured display.
